title: Fast and Stable Gradient Approximation for Quadratic Forms of Hermitian Matrix Functions
claim: Differentiating through the recurrence is unstable without reorthogonalization, while our reuse-forward-quantities gradient stays accurate and stable at all iteration counts.
layout: 2 side-by-side log-scale line plots, shared x-axis, solid vs dashed series
description: Two side-by-side line plots share the x-axis, Lanczos iterations m from 0 to 300, and use log-scale y-axes. The left panel, titled forward error, shows relative error of the quadratic-form approximation. A green solid line (full reorthogonalization) drops steeply to about 1e-13 by m=100 and then plateaus. A purple dashed line (no reorthogonalization) falls much more slowly. The right panel, titled gradient error, compares four series. Blue is ours and orange is the adjoint method. Solid lines use full reorthogonalization and dashed lines use none. All four fall until m≈100. The adjoint with full reorthogonalization then rises to about 1e-6. The orange dashed adjoint without reorthogonalization spikes and blows up above 1e2. Ours stays near 1e-12 with full reorthogonalization, and the dashed blue line shows a gradual decline without it. Legends sit in the top corners of each panel.
caption: Projected and adjoint-based Lanczos gradients [21] for u⊤log(K(θ))u with n = 15,000 and one fixed Rademacher probe. Left: relative error of the quadratic-form approximation. Right: relative gradient error with respect to the kernel hyperparameters. Both panels use dense references.
abstract: Objectives involving quadratic forms $u^*f(A(Î¸))u$ for Hermitian $A$ arise widely in scientific computing and machine learning. Lanczos efficiently approximates these quantities, but differentiating through its recurrence can introduce numerical instability and costly reorthogonalization. Building on existing low-rank Krylov approximations of FrÃ©chet derivatives, we develop a matrix-free gradient implementation that reuses the forward Lanczos quantities without differentiating through the recurrence. We analyze its discrepancy from the exact gradient of the finite Lanczos approximation, deriving an exact residual-coupled error identity and a bound involving the best degree-$(m-1)$ uniform polynomial approximation error of $f'$, multiplied by a basis-sensitivity factor. The discrepancy vanishes when the Krylov subspace is invariant. Experiments demonstrate accurate gradients and runtime improvements over differentiated-Lanczos and modified-Arnoldi baselines. It remains numerically stable without reorthogonalization in all tested settings, including cases where adjoint-based Lanczos differentiation becomes unstable.
